turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on he, she and it with -s?
turns.tutor:
Sure! Watch me solve one first.
Example: "I cook on Saturdays." Now I change "I" to "my dad", which is like "he".
Because the subject is one person, I add -s: "My dad cooks on Saturdays."
So the rule: with he, she or it, the verb takes -s.
Right: He works at a bank. Wrong: He work at a bank.

Your turn now. Write only the verb:
Write the correct form: My sister ___ (play) tennis on Sundays. (answer with only the verb)
